## Keep the common factor {.psf-lesson .split-example}

Take out the highest common factor. Use P and S from inside the bracket.

:::::: {.example-pair}

::::: {.model}

<h3>Worked example</h3>

$6x^2+3x-18$

::: {.fragment}

$=3(2x^2+x-6)$

$P=-12$, $S=1$: opposite signs.

:::

::: {.fragment}

| Pair | $-1,\ 12$ | $-2,\ 6$ | $-3,\ 4$ |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Sum | $11$ | $4$ | $1$ |

:::

::: {.fragment}

Choose $-3,4$: their sum is $1$.

:::

::: {.fragment}

$=3(2x^2+4x-3x-6)$

:::

::: {.fragment}

$=3[2x(x+2)-3(x+2)]$

:::

::: {.fragment}

$=3(2x-3)(x+2)$

:::

:::::

::::: {.paper}

::: {.fragment}

<h3>Your turn</h3>

$6x^2-3x-18$

1. Take out the common factor.
2. Choose the pair.
3. Split and group on paper.

:::

::: {.fragment}

$=3(2x^2-x-6)$

$P=-12$, $S=-1$: opposite signs.

:::

::: {.fragment}

| Pair | $1,\ -12$ | $2,\ -6$ | $3,\ -4$ |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Sum | $-11$ | $-4$ | $-1$ |

:::

::: {.fragment}

Choose $3,-4$: their sum is $-1$.

:::

::: {.fragment}

$=3(2x^2-4x+3x-6)$

:::

::: {.fragment}

$=3[2x(x-2)+3(x-2)]$

:::

::: {.fragment}

$=3(2x+3)(x-2)$

:::

:::::

::::::
